b2-97.title: A school photo project
b2-97.story: Anna's [[photo club]] gave everyone the same task: a [[photo project]] about their own neighborhood. Since Taras switched to [[homeschooling]] this year, Mama let him help and called it his [[art project]] for the month. Max brought his [[drone]] to shoot the park from above. The views looked amazing, but when Anna zoomed in too far, she could see every single [[pixel]]. Her close-up of Grandpa was completely out of [[focus]], so she had to take it again. In the end, the club chose her second try, a warm [[photo portrait]] of Grandpa feeding pigeons, as the best picture of the month. Taras proudly told everyone that he had held the bread.

b2-98.title: At the art museum
b2-98.story: On a rainy Saturday, Anna took her grandparents to the city art museum. Grandma went straight to the hall of French [[impressionism]], where soft light seemed to dance on every canvas. She explained that each [[impressionist]] tried to catch a single moment of light outdoors. Grandpa was confused by [[cubism]]. "Why does this woman have three eyes?" he whispered. In the next room, giant soup cans and comic book faces introduced them to [[pop art]]. The last hall surprised everyone with photos of [[street art]] from Kyiv's walls. Next to them, a big screen showed [[pixel art]] by young game designers. Grandpa admitted that the little square characters were his favorite part of the day.

b2-99.title: Grandma writes a book
b2-99.story: Grandma has always wanted to write a book, and this year she finally started. It is [[nonfiction]]: true stories from her village, mixed with the [[folklore]] her own grandmother used to tell. Anna helped her type the chapters, and Max's sister Sofia, a young [[essayist]] for a student magazine, read the first draft. Sofia was honest and said the opening chapter needed a complete [[rewrite]]. Grandma grumbled, but she spent a whole week on it. To relax, she wrote a short [[haiku]] about the cherry tree outside her window and put it at the start of the book. Last month, a small local [[publisher]] agreed to print it. "It won't join the great [[canon]] of literature," Grandma laughed, "but my great-grandchildren will read it."

b2-100.title: Taras's birthday party
b2-100.story: When Taras turned five, the family argued for weeks about his party. Dad suggested [[laser tag]], until Mama reminded him that the guests were preschoolers. A day at the [[aquapark]] seemed too cold for November, and [[minigolf]] would bore the little ones. In the end, they booked the party room at the [[bowling club]] near their home, with light balls and bumpers for small kids. The real star was a hired [[acrobat]] who flipped across the room and spun a [[hula hoop]] on each arm. Dressed as a cowboy, she caught a toy horse with a [[lasso]], and the kids screamed with joy. Taras got a glowing [[yo-yo]] from Anna and a fidget [[spinner]] from Max. But when Grandpa rolled in a shiny red [[tricycle]], Taras forgot everything else and rode it around until the party ended.

b2-101.title: Game night with Grandpa
b2-101.story: Every Friday, Anna visits her grandparents for game night. Grandpa starts the evening with a [[sudoku]] from the newspaper, which he usually finishes in ten minutes. Then he brings out the old wooden [[backgammon]] board he has had since he was a student. Anna rolled double sixes again and again, but Grandpa kept a perfect [[poker face]], so she never knew if he was worried. Grandma said that luck like that is exactly how people lose all their money at an [[online casino]]: they think it will never end. Sure enough, Anna's luck ran out, and Grandpa won the last game. She just shrugged and said, "Oh well, [[c'est la vie]]." They agreed to split the dishes [[fifty-fifty]] and to play [[croquet]] in the garden as soon as spring came.

b2-102.title: A night out in clubs
b2-102.story: To celebrate the end of their exams, Anna, Max, Lisa, and Ira planned a night out, and each of them chose one place. Ira took them first to a cozy [[jazz club]], where an old trio played quietly by candlelight. Max then dragged everyone to a loud [[rock club]] with sticky floors and a crowd in black T-shirts. Lisa preferred the [[disco club]] next door, where the [[deejay]] played only hits from the seventies. Anna had tickets for a [[techno concert]] in an old factory, but they arrived too late. The main [[techno DJ]] had already finished his two-hour [[DJ set]], and the staff were packing up. On the way back, they passed a dark [[techno club]] with a long line outside, but nobody had the energy to wait. They ended the night at a tiny [[karaoke club]], where Max sang so badly that everyone laughed until two in the morning.

b2-103.title: Max's band needs help
b2-103.story: Max and three friends have a [[cover band]] that plays old hits at school parties. In September their [[bassist]] moved to Lviv, so they urgently needed someone new. Anna's dad, who once played in a student [[jazz band]], offered to help with rehearsals. He also brought Sofia, a talented [[saxophonist]] from her music school, and suddenly they sounded almost like a [[big band]] from an old movie. Finding a new [[bass guitarist]] was harder, because the only boy who came wanted to play songs by his favorite [[boy band]]. Dad made them practice every song with a [[metronome]], since the drummer kept speeding up. At the winter concert, Lisa sang one song alone, and the crowd cheered so loudly that she joked about becoming a [[solo artist]]. Max just smiled, because he had learned the bass lines himself.

b2-104.title: Music on a road trip
b2-104.story: On the long drive to the grandparents' village, the family could not agree on music. Taras wanted [[K-pop]], because he had learned a whole dance from one video. Anna put on her favorite [[indie rock]] playlist, but Mama said it was too sad for a sunny day. Mama chose cheerful [[pop rock]] from the nineties, and Dad switched to old [[rhythm and blues]] as soon as she fell asleep. When Anna teased him, Dad confessed that he had been an [[emo]] at fifteen, with black nail polish and long bangs. Then Anna played a [[dubstep]] track from Max, which made the car shake and woke Mama up at once. Taras announced that he would be a famous [[hip-hop artist]] one day, not some sweet [[pop idol]]. Finally, they all agreed on an old [[rock opera]] that lasted almost as long as the trip. By the time they arrived, everyone was singing the final song together.
